title: SF6 and CFC-12 transit-time ages followed the 1997-2021 oxygen changes on sigma0 26.5 near Bermuda, but did not explain the 2012-2021 loss at 52 W; age noise prevents attribution off California
abstract: Question: are the oxygen losses on the sigma0 = 26.5 density surface at CalCOFI and BATS caused by older water (less ventilation) or by more oxygen use at the same age? Approach: we used CFC-12 and SF6 in GLODAPv2.2023 repeat sections (P02/P03 next to CalCOFI, P02 interior, P16N at 152 W, A22 at 66 W next to BATS, A20 at 52 W; 1985-2021). We calculated inverse-Gaussian transit-time mean ages and compared the AOU change between matched occupations with the oxygen utilization rate (OUR) times the age change. We used a lower OUR (fixed-effect slope) and an upper OUR (AOU divided by age). Results: the sections reproduce the CalCOFI and BATS oxygen changes. Near Bermuda (A22), oxygen fell, rose and fell again (-8.9, +11.3, -18.3 umol/kg for 1997-2003-2012-2021), and the age changed with the same sign (+2.5, -3.5, +5.4 years). With the upper OUR (4.5 umol/kg per year), the residuals were -2.1, +3.2 and -3.2 umol/kg, with intervals that include or touch zero. With the lower OUR, age explains about one quarter. At 52 W (A20), AOU increased by 17.8 umol/kg in 2012-2021 without an age change (-0.3 years); the residual with the upper OUR was +19.3 (8.5 to 30.9). At 152 W, AOU increased by 14.4 in 1991-2015, and the residual with the upper OUR was +7.5 (3.6 to 11.6). Off California, two occupations one year apart differed by 14 years in mean age, so the tracers cannot attribute the CalCOFI oxygen step. Paired SF6 and CFC-12 support a TTD width ratio near 1. Saturation and TTD-shape errors can give false CFC-12 age changes of several years. Limitations: the OUR is only bracketed (bounds differ by 2 to 10 times); there are 3-5 occupations per section and few matched cells; we made no model comparison. Record-level GLODAP data stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Oxygen and TTD mean age on sigma0 = 26.5. (a) North Pacific sections with the CalCOFI offshore annual anomaly; the section values are shifted to start at the CalCOFI value (CCS) or at zero. (b) A22 and A20 occupation means with the BATS annual mean. (c, d) Mean age for each occupation: SF6 where available, else CFC-12 (solid); CFC-12 only (dotted). Occupation means are not matched in space; the 1994 CCS value has 3 casts.

(a) Observed AOU change between consecutive occupations against the ventilation term (OUR x age change). The horizontal bar runs from the lower OUR (open symbol, fixed-effect slope) to the upper OUR (filled symbol, AOU divided by age). Points on the 1:1 line agree with ventilation only. Vertical bars: 95% cell-bootstrap intervals. (b) AOU change against the age change.

TTD checks. (a) Width ratio Delta/Gamma at which SF6 and CFC-12 ages agree, per occupation and density surface (symbol size: number of casts). (b) False CFC-12 age change between the early and late periods under steady flow when the true width ratio differs from the assumed value of 1, and for saturation changes (text).

citations.reason: Source of the CalCOFI annual oxygen anomalies on sigma0 26.5; we test whether its unexplained post-2006 oxygen deficit is a ventilation-age change, and find that the available tracer sections cannot resolve it.
Source of the BATS annual aggregates; the A22 and A20 sections reproduce its oxygen loss on sigma0 26.5 and show that it is part of a gyre-scale swing with age changes of the same sign at 66 W.
